triples.name: climate change mitigation
triples.description: Actions to reduce greenhouse gas emissions or enhance sinks, so that the amount of future warming is limited.

triples.name: climate damage
triples.description: The economic loss caused by climate change relative to a counterfactual world without further warming.

triples.name: mitigation cost
triples.description: The economic cost of reducing greenhouse gas emissions, excluding any avoided climate damage.

triples.name: avoided damage
triples.description: Climate damage that does not occur because emissions were reduced; the benefit side of a mitigation cost benefit analysis.

triples.name: benefit cost ratio
triples.description: Avoided climate damage divided by mitigation cost. Values above one mean that avoiding emissions is cheaper than paying for the consequences.

triples.name: income reduction
triples.description: Reduction of income per capita relative to a baseline without climate impacts.

triples.name: output reduction
triples.description: Reduction of economic output per capita relative to a baseline without further warming.

triples.name: discount rate
triples.description: Rate at which future consumption is valued lower than present consumption in a cost benefit analysis.

triples.name: 1.5 degree target
triples.description: Limiting global mean warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels.

triples.name: 2 degree target
triples.description: Limiting global mean warming to 2 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels.

triples.name: 3.2 degree scenario
triples.description: A scenario with about 3.2 degrees Celsius of global warming by mid century.

triples.name: trillion USD

triples.description: Share of gross domestic product.

triples.description: Share of the countries covered by a study.
